inevitable_need: A gate that sits in front of every agent change: before Claude Code or Cursor touches a service, it knows who owns it, what broke there before and what depends on it, and risky changes get routed to the right human for approval automatically. Not a wiki, an enforced check in the agent's loop.
why_inevitable: We're scaling from a few people running agents to agents opening a meaningful share of PRs, and sooner or later one ships a change into a service it didn't understand and we eat an outage. After that, leadership will demand a pre-change check whether I've picked a tool or not.
must_have: Runs inside the agent workflow (MCP or CI hook) and can block or require human approval, not just advise
Ownership, prior incidents and blast radius pulled from our real repos, Slack and incident history, with citations I can check
Self-hostable or a data-handling story that passes our security review without months of back-and-forth
deal_breakers: Per-seat pricing across the whole engineering org when only a handful of people and agents drive the value
Confidently wrong ownership or blast-radius answers with no sources, so engineers learn to ignore it
Sending Slack, Drive and incident data to an early-stage hosted service with no SOC 2 or clear retention and access controls
expected_provider: Probably a new startup or our own platform team stitching it together. The agent makers will add basic permission prompts, but they won't own our cross-tool org context, and GitHub or our incident tool will only see their own slice.
memoryworks_would_need: Make the agent briefing an enforceable gate with approval routing, not just context, and prove on a self-hosted pilot that its owner and blast-radius answers are right with citations. Then price it per repo or per agent with a security posture finance and security can sign off on, not $20 per engineer for the whole org.
